submission.justification: Algorithm-L3 gives the highest signal efficiency in the emulation at the allocated 8 kHz rate. Scanning thresholds: 20 GeV 86.3%, 25 GeV 91.5%, 30 GeV 91.8%, 35 GeV 91.0%, 45 GeV 89.7%. The best value is at 30 GeV. The 2025 summary agrees on the ranking at 35 GeV (L3 92%, L1 85%, L2 74%). However, the 4.0 us FPGA latency limit is a hard constraint and I could not verify it. No document in the project gives latency for any candidate, and the tools do not report it. L3 is an iterative topological clustering algorithm, which may be slower than the others, so the latency check is the main risk. This recommendation is conditional: L3 at 30 GeV should be adopted only after its measured FPGA latency is confirmed to be at or below 4.0 us. If it exceeds that limit, the fallback is Algorithm-L1, which is the next-best candidate at 85% efficiency at 35 GeV. Its latency is also unverified.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be one of the three candidates in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L3 is one of the listed candidates.

requirements.requirement: FPGA latency must not exceed 4.0 us (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: No project document reports latency for any candidate (candidate_specs.md only says all fit the resource budget). The simulation tool returns only efficiency. Verification is required before adoption; L3 may be slower due to its iterative clustering.
Recommended threshold is 30 GeV, inside the 20-60 GeV range.

requirements.requirement: Highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated rate (8 kHz)
requirements.evidence: L3 at 30 GeV gives 91.76% efficiency, the highest of the scanned L3 thresholds, and higher than L1 (84.97%) and L2 (73.78%) at 35 GeV. The tool reports efficiency at the allocated rate; the rate itself was not independently reported.
